statements: 80 FP 74.03 19.3 Top-1 (%) arXiv:2610.23046v1 [cs.NE] 16 Oct 2026 {kai.sun1, peibo.duan, levin.kuhlmann}@monash.edu On neuromorphic chips, spiking neural networks (SNNs) consume far less energy than artificial neural networks (ANNs), but the limited memory of these chips requires low-bit synaptic weights and membrane potentials.
Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods provide them without retraining and, like those for ANNs, minimize numerical errors such as the mean squared error (MSE).
In an SNN, however, a quantization error reaches later layers only through the spikes it flips.
